questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a sound-and-meaning compound lets you predict
questions.learningObjective: State what a sound-meaning compound predicts
questions.stem: In an architect's brief, a sound-and-meaning compound is described; what can it help you predict about a new character?

options.text: It predicts a rough pronunciation from the sound part.
It predicts the exact stroke count of the character.
options.misconception: confuses sound part with stroke counter

options.text: It predicts the radical's dictionary page only.
It predicts nothing at all about the character.

questions.explanation: A sound-meaning compound hints at pronunciation through its sound part. It does not give stroke count or page.

provenance.author: bank-team-chinese
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: A component written twice or three times
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a component may be doubled
questions.stem: An architect's brief notes the same component written twice in one character; explain why that happens.

answer.exemplar: The component is repeated to build a larger character, often keeping the same radical family while expanding meaning or sound.

questions.explanation: Repetition builds compound characters from a base component. It is a structural, not accidental, choice.

provenance.author: bank-team-chinese
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Codes that record a character's structure

stimulus.body: An architect's brief mentions codes that record how a character is built from components and strokes.

questions.stem: What do such codes primarily record?

options.text: The character's pronunciation in every dialect.
The character's stroke count and component layout.
The historical dynasty of the character.
The color of the ink used to write it.

questions.explanation: Structural codes record stroke count and component layout. They are not pronunciation, history, or ink color.

questions.subject: CHINESE
